issues.legal_issue: A resident of an area protected by a statutory planning scheme may seek enforcement of the scheme against a municipal approval that conflicts with it before the approved use is actually carried out.
material_facts: The challenger resided in the residential area where a building was approved for conversion into a cinema theatre.
The planning scheme was intended to benefit residents and regulated the uses permitted in the area.
The municipality approved the conversion despite the scheme’s restrictions, and the challenger sought to have that approval set aside.
issues.conclusion: The resident had a right to insist that the municipality perform its duty to observe the scheme and could challenge the approval at the threshold, without waiting for the building to be used as a cinema.
issues.legal_principle: A resident with a special and substantial interest in the performance of a statutory duty may seek to compel a public authority to comply with it. A planning scheme serves the residents of the locality, and an unauthorized construction may materially affect their enjoyment of property. The Court distinguished a claim for damages for breach of statutory duty, for which the principles discussed in Cutler v. Wandsworth Stadium [1949] A.C. 398 applied. It also relied on Yabbicom v. King [1899] 1 Q.B. 444 for the principle that approval of plans contrary to applicable building rules is illegal and inoperative.

rule.if: resident_challenge_to_municipal_approval and challenger_resides_in_affected_area and statutory_scheme_protects_local_residents and municipal_action_conflicts_with_scheme

predicates.resident_challenge_to_municipal_approval: A resident brings a challenge to a municipal approval affecting the locality.
predicates.challenger_resides_in_affected_area: The challenger resides in the area affected by the proposed use or construction.
predicates.statutory_scheme_protects_local_resident: A statutory planning scheme regulates development for the benefit of residents in the area.
predicates.municipal_action_conflicts_with_scheme: The municipality takes action that is inconsistent with the planning scheme.

issues.definition: When a resident challenges municipal action conflicting with a scheme that protects the area’s residents, the resident may seek enforcement before the approved use has begun.

issues.legal_issue: A municipality cannot approve a cinema in a residential area contrary to a planning scheme that restricts where such premises may be located.
material_facts: The planning scheme classified a theatre as business premises and restricted such premises to places reserved for that purpose.
The scheme limited the uses of the area to residential purposes, subject to specified permitted uses and required approvals.
The building had originally been licensed as a marriage hall and lecture hall, and the municipality later approved its conversion into a cinema without the required authority under the scheme.
The municipality had previously refused permission to construct a cinema theatre building at the site.
issues.conclusion: The municipal resolution approving the conversion had no legal foundation and was quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Under the Madras Town Planning Act, 1920, the planning scheme governed permitted uses in the area. Clauses 14 and 15 restricted uses and provided for the locations and approvals required for business premises, including theatres. The municipality could not disregard, vary, or modify the scheme by approving a prohibited use. Consistent with Yabbicom v. King [1899] 1 Q.B. 444, approval contrary to applicable planning restrictions is illegal and inoperative.

rule.if: appeal_challenging_municipal_resolution and proposed_use_conflicts_with_planning_scheme and required_planning_approval_is_absent and municipality_cannot_change_scheme

predicates.appeal_challenging_municipal_resolution: A party appeals against a municipal resolution approving a proposed development or use.
predicates.proposed_use_conflicts_with_planning_sch: The proposed development or use is prohibited or restricted at the site by the applicable planning scheme.
predicates.required_planning_approval_is_absent: An approval required by the planning scheme for the proposed development or use has not been obtained.
predicates.municipality_cannot_change_scheme: The municipality has no authority to vary or modify the planning scheme.

issues.definition: An approval challenged on appeal must be quashed when the proposed use conflicts with the planning scheme, required approval is absent, and the municipality cannot change the scheme.

issues.legal_issue: Acquiescence or expenditure incurred in reliance on a municipal approval cannot validate an exercise of power that exceeds statutory authority.
material_facts: The High Court accepted that the municipal resolution approving conversion of the building into a cinema violated the planning scheme.
The High Court nevertheless left that resolution undisturbed because the beneficiary was said to have spent a substantial sum of money.
On appeal, the Supreme Court set aside the High Court’s decision and quashed the resolution.
issues.conclusion: The resolution could not be saved by the beneficiary’s expenditure or by acquiescence, and it had to be quashed.
issues.legal_principle: An excess of statutory power cannot be validated by acquiescence or estoppel, and a court will not assist a person in avoiding express statutory requirements. The Court relied on Maddison v. Alderson [1883] 8 App. Cas. 467 for the principle that courts will not permit a statute to be used as an instrument of fraud.

predicates.appeal_from_refusal_to_quash_municipal_r: An appeal challenges a decision that left a municipal resolution in force instead of quashing it.
predicates.municipal_resolution_exceeds_statutory_p: The municipal resolution authorizes action beyond the powers granted to the municipality.
predicates.beneficiary_incurred_expenses_or_receive: The beneficiary spent money in reliance on the resolution or another person acquiesced in it.

issues.definition: A resolution that exceeds municipal authority remains invalid despite expenditure or acquiescence when an appeal challenges the refusal to quash it.
